reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker instructs viewers to buy Strong tokens, connect a wallet, and create nodes by paying a 10-STRONG contribution and recurring maintenance fee. The participation is promoted through recurring rewards and the prospect of substantial income or living off the earnings, with the speaker saying the fee will eventually pay for itself. Although rewards are described as variable and not guaranteed and no referral link is provided, the video still promotes a paid income-generating participation process.

citations.quote: you need 10 coins minimum
it will cost you 14.95 us dollars to be able to um purchase this note every month
it's just another way of earning passive income
they're going to continuously pay me and my rewards will go up
i will be able to open another node so i'm going to use my node money to open other nodes

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful uncertainty rather than a guaranteed-profit promise. The StrongBlock screen states that rewards are calculated using multiple factors and are variable and not guaranteed. That qualification matters: the speaker describes his own expected outcome, but the supplied material does not establish that viewers were promised a fixed return. The video also identifies recurring costs and transaction fees, giving viewers information about the financial conditions instead of concealing them. On this record, the content can be read as a qualified discussion of a volatile crypto activity, not deceptive certification of an assured income stream.

citations.quote: it will cost you 14.95 us dollars to be able to um purchase this note every month
there's a small fee
my rewards will go up

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening emphasizes the 10-STRONG requirement and monthly fee, but those facts establish a paid service, not deception. It also treats the speaker's optimistic language as dispositive while omitting the on-screen qualification that rewards are variable and not guaranteed. The statement that the fee may eventually be covered is an expressed expectation, not proof of a guaranteed return or concealed condition.

citations.quote: once you get to a certain amount it just pays for itself
you need 10 coins minimum

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification does not neutralize the central solicitation. The speaker still tells viewers to acquire Strong, create a node, and pay recurring fees while presenting the activity as passive income. The screen's variable-reward language identifies uncertainty in the amount, but it does not remove the paid participation mechanism or the income-oriented pitch.

citations.quote: it's just another way of earning passive income
they're going to continuously pay me and my rewards will go up

opening.argument: The video's dominant format is an operational walkthrough of the speaker's own setup. He screen-shares the wallet and service, explains how to connect them, selects a node, accepts the terms, and completes the creation process. That is concrete instruction about using a blockchain application, not merely a bare demand to send money. The supplied frames likewise show a node-creation interface and a confirmation that the node was created. A tutorial can describe the speaker's expected rewards without becoming a deceptive investment guarantee; the evidence supports an educational demonstration of a process the speaker personally followed.

citations.quote: I'm going to do a screen share with you guys. I'm going to show you about this node that I'm going to activate.
i'm going to show you how easy this is to start a node
You press create node. This does everything for you.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not change what the tutorial teaches. The walkthrough specifically directs viewers through acquiring the token, creating a node, and paying the associated charges, while repeatedly describing the resulting rewards and income. Demonstrating a transaction can still promote the underlying paid opportunity; instructional format alone does not make the financial claims accurate.

citations.quote: you buy some Strongcoins, then you come to StrongBlock
I'm gonna create a node
I can produce a large amount of income for myself

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstration is not neutral instruction. It is paired with an invitation to reproduce the setup and a claimed path to passive income, including compounding rewards into additional nodes. Showing the interface and a creation confirmation proves only that a node-creation workflow was displayed; it does not prove that the promised income exists or that participation is safe.

citations.quote: There is no referral link, you can simply just do this whenever you feel like it.
once i get these rewards to 10 i will be able to open another node

opening.argument: The evidence is also consistent with ordinary purchase of a blockchain service: the speaker exchanges cryptocurrency for Strong, pays a stated Ethereum transaction fee, and agrees to a recurring maintenance charge. The video does not show a recruitment hierarchy, a request for passwords or private keys, or a referral commission. Indeed, the speaker expressly says, “There is no referral link,” and says viewers can undertake the process independently. Those details distinguish a disclosed service transaction from a classic deceptive recruitment scheme. The material may describe a risky or speculative product, but risk or an unfavorable outcome is not by itself proof of a scam.

citations.quote: i just swapped my e-file very simple for strong
There is no referral link, you can simply just do this whenever you feel like it.
you know, on Ethereum blockchain, it is custom tokens there are ECR20 tokens

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a referral link does not answer the paid-node issue. The reference does not need to prove a downline or credential theft: it identifies a required token contribution, recurring maintenance payment, and rewards tied to node participation. Describing those payments as ordinary commerce does not explain why the speaker presents them as a way to generate passive income and fund more nodes.

citations.quote: you need 10 coins minimum
it's just another way of earning passive income
i will be able to open another node so i'm going to use my node money to open other nodes

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A transaction can look like ordinary commerce and still be a paid-return scheme. The relevant combination is the required 10 STRONG contribution, monthly maintenance, and promised or anticipated rewards, not whether recruitment or password theft is shown. The no-referral statement narrows one mechanism but does not disprove the income-generating node mechanism documented in the video.
